title: Battle of Midway's hidden radio glitch that turned the tide
hook: A broken Japanese radio transmission gave the Allies the decisive edge at the Battle of Midway.
description:
A broken Japanese radio transmission gave the Allies the decisive edge at the Battle of Midway. Discover the hidden glitch that changed history.

beats.say: You never heard how a broken Japanese radio set changed Midway's fate for the allies.
On June 4, 1942, a stray transmission revealed the Japanese fleet's exact position to U.S. scouts.
The U.S. codebreakers, led by Commander Joseph Rochefort, used that clue to launch a daring ambush.
While Admiral Fletcher's carriers steamed north, a lone PBY patrol plane spotted the Japanese carriers looming.
At 10:22 a.m., dive-bombers from USS Enterprise crashed into Akagi's deck, igniting a fiery inferno.
The Japanese lost four carriers-Akagi, Kaga, Soryu, and Hiryu-within minutes, crippling their air power.

beats.say: What many ignore: the U.S. lost 307 men, a tragic price that silenced the Pacific's roar.
The battle's turning point wasn't the planes, but a mis-read Japanese signal that delayed their counterattack.
That delay let the U.S. carriers strike again, sinking the last Japanese carrier, Hiryu, at dusk.
Midway proved a single miscommunication could tip a war, reshaping the Pacific forever.
